hazard_indicator: High UTCI Days (ERA5-HEAT; count of days with a Universal Thermal Climate Index above 32 degrees)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the only available index measures human thermal comfort rather than asset-level heat stress, and it is reanalysis-based with no climate projections available

hazard_granularity: 0.25 degree grid (~28km); 0.11 degree grid for Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days
hazard_indicator: Hot Days, Tropical Nights, Warmest Three Day Period, Climatological Heatwave Days and Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days
coverage_rationale: Full because several dedicated heatwave indices with documented percentile thresholds are provided; the apparent-temperature variant comes from a different input dataset and is therefore not directly comparable with the others

hazard_indicator: Fire Weather Index and High Fire Danger Days (days with FWI above 30, EFFIS classification)
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated fire-danger indices are provided; the resolution is finer than that of most other indices in this source, which come from a different input dataset

hazard_indicator: Extreme Wind Speed Days (days above the 98th percentile of 10m wind speed)
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated wind-extremes index is provided; it is threshold-based and does not identify individual windstorm events

hazard_indicator: Aridity Actual (ratio of actual evapotranspiration to precipitation)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the only available index describes the climatic water balance and not water stress in the sense of demand relative to available supply

hazard_indicator: Flood Recurrence (50-year return-period discharge) and River Discharge
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated river-flooding indices from a hydrological model are provided; the resolution is finer than that of the atmospheric indices in this source, and coverage is limited to riverine flooding

hazard_indicator: Maximum Consecutive Five-Day Precipitation, Extreme Precipitation Total and Extreme Precipitation Days
coverage_rationale: Full because three dedicated extreme-precipitation indices with documented percentile thresholds are provided

hazard_granularity: 0.25 degree grid (~28km) for the meteorological indices; 5km grid for the soil-moisture index
hazard_indicator: Meteorological Drought Duration and Magnitude (SPI-3), Consecutive Dry Days and Mean Soil Moisture
coverage_rationale: Full because both meteorological and soil-moisture drought indices are provided; they come from different input datasets, so their resolutions differ and they are not directly comparable

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, heat wave category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it

hazard_indicator: Risk Analysis layer for wildfire, derived from EFFIS data and the wildland-urban interface
coverage_rationale: Full because a modelled hazard layer is provided in the Risk Analysis module and aggregated to administrative units

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, windstorm category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it

hazard_indicator: Risk Analysis layer for river and coastal flood, based on the JRC pan-European flood hazard maps
coverage_rationale: Full because a modelled hazard layer is provided in the Risk Analysis module and aggregated to administrative units; riverine and coastal flooding are covered, pluvial flooding is not

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, flash flood category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, drought category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it

hazard_granularity: 200m to 5km grid, finer than the NUTS 2/3 granularity of the other layers
hazard_indicator: Risk Analysis layer for landslide, based on the European Landslide Susceptibility Map ELSUS v2 combined with GPCC precipitation data
coverage_rationale: Full because a modelled susceptibility layer is provided; its resolution is finer than that of the other layers in this source, which are aggregated to administrative units

hazard_granularity: approximately 8km (ECMWF forecast) to 28km (GEOS-5 forecast); 250m for burnt-area perimeters
hazard_indicator: Fire Weather Index in six danger classes (daily forecast raster) and burnt-area perimeters from the Rapid Damage Assessment
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated fire-danger and burnt-area products are provided; the forecast grid is coarse relative to Austria, and the index is time-varying, so a static exposure attribute requires an own aggregation choice

hazard_indicator: No named index; ERA5 soil temperature at four depth levels, as raw variables
coverage_rationale: Partial because no ready-made permafrost index exists in the catalogue; the raw variables are usable only as input to the institution’s own model

hazard_indicator: Raw 2m temperature variables (daily minimum, maximum and mean); the derived heatwave indices are published separately as the ECDE indicators dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the temperature fields are the quantity that defines the hazard; the threshold and the index definition rest with the institution, and ready-made indices are reached through the separate ECDE dataset

hazard_indicator: Raw 10m wind-speed variables; the derived Extreme Wind Speed Days index is published separately as part of the ECDE indicators dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the wind-speed fields are the quantity that defines the hazard; the threshold definition rests with the institution, and the ready-made index is reached through the separate ECDE dataset

hazard_indicator: Raw total-precipitation variables; the derived extreme-precipitation indices are published separately as part of the ECDE indicators dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the precipitation fields are the quantity that defines the hazard; the threshold and the index definition rest with the institution, and ready-made indices are reached through the separate ECDE dataset

hazard_indicator: Raw precipitation variables from which SPI-3 can be derived; the soil-moisture component is published separately in the hydrology dataset
coverage_rationale: Partial because the meteorological component must be derived by the institution and the soil-moisture component belongs to a separate ready-made dataset

hazard_indicator: No named index; raw precipitation, soil-moisture and wind-speed variables
coverage_rationale: Partial because no erosion index exists in the catalogue; using the source requires independent erosion modelling, for example of the RUSLE type

hazard_indicator: Physical-risk indicators aggregated from Pillar 3 ESG disclosures, published per institution and as EU aggregates
coverage_rationale: Partial because the dashboard reports supervisory statistics on exposures flagged as subject to physical risk; it is not spatially resolved and cannot be attached to an individual exposure

hazard_indicator: Physical-risk indicators aggregated from Pillar 3 ESG disclosures, published per institution and as EU aggregates

hazard_indicator: Modelled inundation areas HQ30, HQ100 and HQ300 (Hochwasserueberflutungsflaechen)
coverage_rationale: Full because the dataset is the official modelled inundation extent for the 30-, 100- and 300-year events, maintained under the implementation of the Floods Directive

hazard_granularity: Hazard zone polygons, delineated by technical criteria independently of parcel boundaries; can be intersected with parcel or address locations
hazard_indicator: Red and yellow hazard zones for torrent processes (Wildbach)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the plan covers torrent-related flood only, and is mapped only for municipalities with torrent, avalanche or erosion catchments and only within the spatially relevant area

hazard_granularity: Hazard zone polygons, delineated by technical criteria independently of parcel boundaries; can be intersected with parcel or address locations
hazard_indicator: Red and yellow hazard zones for erosion processes
coverage_rationale: Full because the hazard type is assessed in its own right. Mapped only for municipalities that contain torrent, avalanche or erosion catchments and only within the spatially relevant area, so an unmapped location is ambiguous

hazard_granularity: Hazard zone polygons, delineated by technical criteria independently of parcel boundaries; can be intersected with parcel or address locations
hazard_indicator: Hazard depiction for rockfall and landslide processes (Steinschlag, Rutschungen)
coverage_rationale: Full because the hazard type is assessed in its own right. Mapped only for municipalities that contain torrent, avalanche or erosion catchments and only within the spatially relevant area, so an unmapped location is ambiguous

hazard_indicator: Daily wind-gust maps for Austria, provided through the cooperation with GeoSphere Austria
coverage_rationale: Full in the sense that Austria-wide wind information is available, but it describes current conditions rather than a long-term hazard zoning, and its grid is coarser than the parcel-level flood layer

hazard_granularity: Parcel/cadastral level; HORA 3D additionally simulates flood depth at building level
hazard_indicator: Gefahrendarstellung Fliessgewaesser: flood hazard zoning for the 30-, 100- and 300-year event, including inundation zones of standing waters
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated Austria-wide flood hazard zoning is provided and can be queried for any address; it is published for first orientation and is not a legally binding hazard zone plan

hazard_indicator: Landslide susceptibility screening layer, provided through the cooperation with GeoSphere Austria
coverage_rationale: Partial because the layer is an indicative screening product, newer and less mature than the flood layer, and is provided on a grid rather than at parcel level

hazard_indicator: Baseline Water Stress, Baseline Water Depletion, Interannual Variability, Seasonal Variability and Groundwater Table Decline
coverage_rationale: Full because several dedicated water-stress indicators are provided, each as a raw value, a score on a scale from 0 to 5 and a category label; they are modelled with PCR-GLOBWB 2 and describe demand relative to available supply

hazard_indicator: Riverine Flood Risk and Coastal Flood Risk indicators
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated flood indicators are provided in their own right rather than inferred from the water-stress indicators; they express expected annual affected population and assets, not inundation depth

hazard_indicator: Drought Risk indicator
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated drought indicator is provided; it combines hazard, exposure and vulnerability into a risk score rather than describing the meteorological drought itself
